mcq.q: Why are carry look-ahead adders (CLA) preferred over ripple-carry adders for large bit sizes?

options.C: They compute carries in parallel, reducing delay.

mcq.q: A full adder can be constructed using:
Which of the following statements about ripple-carry adders is TRUE?

options.A: They produce the final sum in one clock cycle regardless of bit size.
options.B: The carry-out of one stage becomes the carry-in of the next stage, causing delay.
options.C: Ripple-carry adders are faster than carry look-ahead adders.
options.D: Ripple-carry adders use fewer gates than half adders.

mcq.answer_text: The carry-out of one stage becomes the carry-in of the next stage, causing delay.

sq.q: Why is a Carry Look-Ahead Adder faster than a Ripple-Carry Adder?
answer: A Carry Look-Ahead Adder (CLA) computes all carry outputs in parallel using Generate (G = A·B) and Propagate (P = A ⊕ B) signals, avoiding sequential carry propagation and thus reducing delay.
